reference_metadata.case_name: Ford Nano 2.7L/3.0L EcoBoost Intake Valve Hardness
reference_metadata.note: This file defines the source-grounded benchmark inputs and expected result before solver execution. It is not the frozen reference artifact.

variable.meaning: Hardness value associated with the drawing-controlled valve-tip hardened zone and the documented SCCAF Tip Hardness characteristic.
variable.measurement_alignment_note: Historical SCCAF production control used Rockwell C indentation on the valve tip. Ford Central Laboratory later measured Vickers microindentation hardness on a metallographic section and converted those values to Rockwell C according to ASTM E140. The laboratory measurements are evidence of physically observed hardness states, not historical production inspection records.

evidence.supports: Historical SCCAF Tip Hardness specification was 50 min HRC, using a Rockwell Hardness Tester, with sampling at start of shift and tool change/changeover.
Ford states that the SCCAF did not detail an upper tolerance limit for valve tip hardness until September 7, 2021.
JT4E-6507-AB launched with a tip-hardness specification of 50 MIN and the tip-hardness specification changed to 50-57 HRC in October 2020.
Field-failure valves were reported with hardness above the maximum 57 HRC specification, including measurements described in the 58-60 HRC range near the keeper-groove region.
Historical hardness verification was performed only on the valve tip; profile and keeper-groove hardness verification were subsequently added.
The investigation records the belief that measured tip hardness represented the rest of the tip-hardened zone; this finding is excluded from the primary one-variable acceptance-boundary model.
Ford Central Laboratory report US231121 analyzes two fractured intake valves, including Intake Valve 10, from warranty-return vehicles.

The report states that Ford Drawing JT4E-6507-AB specifies 50-57 HRC in the applicable hardened region and reports Intake Valve 10 measurements including 58, 59, and 60 HRC, with out-of-specification markings.
The core hardness traverse for Intake Valve 10 also contains values above the 57 HRC upper specification.

historical_verification_V_old.name: Historical manufacturing process-control acceptance
historical_verification_V_old.scope_note: V_old represents the documented historical SCCAF process-control acceptance criterion, not the Ford engineering drawing.

observed_feasible_subset_F_obs.name: Source-grounded observed hardness envelope
observed_feasible_subset_F_obs.semantics_note: The interval 58-60 HRC is used as the envelope of source-grounded observed hardness values. It does not claim that every real-valued hardness between 58 and 60 HRC was individually measured, nor that this interval is the entire manufacturing feasible domain.

verification_question.quantified_expression: exists H: F_obs(H) AND V_old(H) AND NOT R(H)
verification_question.expanded_expression: exists H: (58 <= H <= 60) AND (H >= 50) AND NOT(50 <= H <= 57)

expected_result.note: No exact witness value is preselected. Any solver witness inside the frozen witness class is acceptable if it satisfies the frozen formal model.

interpretation.primary_claim: The engineering hardness specification contained a 57 HRC upper bound, while the documented historical production process-control criterion did not include that upper bound. Source-grounded fractured hardware contains hardness values above 57 HRC. The benchmark asks whether a state exists inside the observed hardness envelope that satisfies the historical process-control acceptance criterion while violating the engineering requirement.

secondary_findings_excluded_from_primary.name: Representativeness / Relationship Gap
secondary_findings_excluded_from_primary.description: Historical tip-only hardness checking was treated as representative of the wider hardened zone, while later investigation added profile and keeper-groove checks.
secondary_findings_excluded_from_primary.reason_excluded: This is a spatial/representativeness relationship problem and is intentionally kept separate from the primary one-variable acceptance-boundary benchmark.

do_not_claim: Do not claim that every 58-60 HRC valve actually passed historical production inspection.
Do not claim that a 58, 59, or 60 HRC value was measured during historical production inspection and recorded as PASS.
Do not claim that hardness was the sole cause of valve fracture.
Do not claim that every recalled vehicle contained a 58-60 HRC valve.
Do not describe the historical SCCAF as the Ford engineering drawing.
Do not claim that Ford or NHTSA formally identified a Verification Escape or Z3 counterexample; that formalization belongs to this project.
Do not describe F_obs as the full manufacturing feasible domain.
Do not claim that the Ford Central Laboratory microindentation measurements are identical measurement events or identical test methods to the historical SCCAF Rockwell production measurements.
